questions.q: Which shortcut **copies the contents of the cell above** into the active cell?
questions.solution: **Ctrl+D = fill down** (from the cell above); **Ctrl+R = fill right**.

questions.q: Multiprogramming means:
options: Several programs kept in memory with the CPU switching among them
questions.solution: In multiprogramming, multiple programs reside in main memory and the single CPU switches to another whenever the current one waits (e.g. for I/O), raising CPU utilisation. It does not require multiple CPUs or users.
questions.shortcut: One CPU, many resident programs = multiprogramming; time-sliced fairness = time-sharing.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a web browser?
questions.solution: Yahoo is a web portal/search engine, not browser software. Opera, Safari and Firefox are browsers.
questions.shortcut: Scan for the service/brand that you cannot install as a program - that is the odd one.

questions.q: In an odd-one-out list, which item does NOT belong with the others?
questions.solution: Virus, trojan, worm are **malware (attacks)**; a firewall is **protection** — the odd one out.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: **Succeeded**: succeed is one of the three -ceed verbs (proceed, succeed, exceed), so it keeps **-ceed** before -ed. It also has double c.

questions.q:
Select the word which is most opposite in meaning to the given word.

VIRTUE
questions.solution: *Virtue* = moral goodness → its standard opposite is **vice** (moral fault). 'Value' drifts to worth, and the v-initial 'virtuosity/vigour' are shape decoys.
questions.shortcut: Kill the v-initial decoys; pick the genuine moral opposite.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.
questions.solution: Subjects ending in -ics (mathematics, physics, economics) take a singular verb → **is**.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom in bold.

Meena was **on cloud nine** when she cleared the exam.
questions.solution: Clearing an exam is good news, so the meaning must be positive. *On cloud nine* = **extremely happy**.
questions.shortcut: Good-news sentence → pick the only happy option.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT true about Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs)?
options: They are registered under Section 45-IA of the RBI Act, 1934
They can lend and make investments
They can issue cheques to their customers
DICGC insurance does not cover their deposits
questions.solution: NBFCs **cannot issue cheques** because they lie outside the payment and settlement system. The other statements are true: registration under Section 45-IA, lending rights, and no DICGC cover.
questions.shortcut: The NBFC's three 'noes': no demand deposits, no cheques, no DICGC.

questions.q: **Vinegar** is a solution of about 5–8% —
questions.solution: Vinegar = dilute **acetic acid (CH₃COOH)**, made by fermenting ethanol. Citric acid is lemon's; formic acid is the ant sting's.

questions.q: India's first biosphere reserve, set up in 1986, is:
questions.solution: The **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve** (1986) spans Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka at the junction of the Western and Eastern Ghats. Gulf of Mannar and Nanda Devi came in the later lists.

questions.q: The song ***Vande Mataram*** occurs in Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's novel —
questions.solution: ***Anandamath* (1882)** contains Vande Mataram; Tagore first sang it at the **1896 Calcutta session** of the Congress.

questions.q: The ratio of two numbers is 7 : 11 and their product is 693. The sum of the numbers is:
In a workforce of 4,800, the pie chart shows two departments occupying 15% and 25% of the circle. The number of employees in these two departments together is:
questions.shortcut: Add the shares first: 40% of 4800 = 1920. One multiplication, not two.

questions.q: A swimmer swims at 12 km/h in still water and the current runs at 3 km/h. The time she takes to swim 30 km downstream is:
If $x-y=2$ and $y-z=3$, then the value of $(x-y)^3+(y-z)^3+(z-x)^3$ is:
questions.solution: Brackets sum to 0 → cube-sum $= 3(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)$. $z-x = -5$ → $3\times2\times3\times(-5) = -90$.

questions.q: Arrange as in a dictionary: **Colonel, Colony, Column, Colour, Colossus.** Which word comes **just after Colony**?
questions.solution: All share COL. 4th letters: o (Colonel, Colony, Colour, Colossus) vs u (Column) → the o-group first. 5th letters: n (Colonel, Colony), s (Colossus), u (Colour); n < s < u. The n-pair: 6th letters e (Colonel) vs y (Colony) → Colonel, Colony. Full order: Colonel, Colony, Colossus, Colour, Column → just after Colony = **Colossus**.
questions.shortcut: u sends Column last; inside the o-group sort 5th letters n < s < u.

questions.q: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.solution: There are 3 rows, so 9 smallest triangles. Upright triangles of every size: 10. Upside-down triangles: 3. Total = 10 + 3 = **13**.

questions.q:
Three of the following four number-sets are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd set.
(**NOTE:** Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking them into their digits. For example, with 13 you may add, subtract or multiply 13 itself, but you may not split it into 1 and 3.)

**(5, 34, 3), (4, 25, 3), (6, 61, 5), (7, 50, 2)**
questions.shortcut: Middle larger than the product of the outer numbers → try sum of squares.

questions.q: Select the related letters: **CFIL : DHLP :: GJMP : ?**
questions.solution: The shifts rise: C+1 = D, F+2 = H, I+3 = L, L+4 = P — tuple (+1, +2, +3, +4). Apply it to GJMP: G+1 = H, J+2 = L, M+3 = P, P+4 = T → **HLPT**.
questions.shortcut: Copy the whole tuple exactly; do not average or 'tidy' it.
